channel.title: Threat Desk
channel.description: Vulnerabilities, advisories and threat activity, twice a day

item.title: Ghostscript sandbox escape enables RCE via crafted file uploads
item.description: Security firm pwn.ai demonstrated that a now-patched Ghostscript flaw allows crafted file uploads to escape the sandbox and execute remote code on Linux servers.

item.title: OpenRouter removes three providers after prompt theft
item.description: Researchers at Dragos discovered that attackers stole data from three AI inference providers for months, including requests marked as Zero Data Retention.

item.title: Bulgaria reveals five-year government data breach
item.description: Bulgarian authorities discovered a cyberespionage campaign active since 2021 that exfiltrated 130 GB of sensitive state documents, highlighting critical gaps in national security monitoring.

item.title: Dell patches critical 9.9 flaw in Enterprise SONiC
item.description: A critical argument injection vulnerability in Dell Enterprise SONiC allows low-privileged remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands on network switches.

item.title: Bots exploit leaked AWS keys in Docker images within eight seconds
item.description: Researchers found that automated scanners identify and use credentials left in public container images almost instantly, highlighting a critical gap in registry security.

item.title: US investigates potential Iranian link in FortiGate breaches of 50 commercial ships
item.description: US authorities are investigating whether Iranian state actors exploited known Fortinet FortiGate flaws to access the operational technology networks of up to 50 commercial vessels.

item.title: Fake .NET job assessments used to spread malware via NuGet
item.description: Researchers found 13 malicious NuGet packages disguised as coding assessments that steal credentials and establish remote access on Windows developer machines.

item.title: CISA adds Drupal, Idunno, and Optimizely flaws to KEV catalogue
item.description: CISA has listed three actively exploited vulnerabilities, including a critical Drupal core flaw, in its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue, setting a 27 November deadline for federal agencies.

item.title: FinCEN takes systems offline after unauthorised access
item.description: The US Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network has taken some systems offline as a precaution following a cybersecurity incident involving unauthorised access to a limited subset of its infrastructure.

item.title: GnuPG releases fix for critical GPGME memory corruption flaw
item.description: A malicious OpenPGP key can trigger a double-free condition in GPGME, potentially allowing remote attackers to execute arbitrary code or crash applications.

item.title: CERT-In warns of AI-assisted attacks causing unauthorised payments
item.description: India's CERT-In has issued an advisory stating that AI-assisted cyber attacks are targeting ICT assets, resulting in unauthorised financial transactions at banking and fintech entities.

item.title: Critical ScreenConnect flaw exploited to hijack MSP technician PCs
item.description: Threat actors are actively exploiting CVE-2026-84869 in ConnectWise ScreenConnect to execute malicious payloads on technician hosts, bypassing standard session controls.

item.title: Critical code injection flaw in binary-parser library
item.description: A critical vulnerability in the binary-parser library allows attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript by manipulating parser definitions.

item.title: US lawmakers propose CISA board to review major cyber incidents
item.description: A new bill seeks to establish a National Cyber and AI Investigations Board within CISA to analyse root causes of significant cyber incidents without assigning liability.

item.title: VMware 0-Day and Java4Shell featured in weekly security recap
item.description: The Hacker News highlights a week of critical vulnerabilities including a VMware zero-day and Java4Shell, illustrating how small openings lead to major breaches.

item.title: Trump to nominate Kirsten Davies as US National Cyber Director
item.description: The White House intends to appoint the Pentagon’s chief information officer to the role permanently following strong industry support.

item.title: Bots spoof AI agent names to hunt for secrets
item.description: Cequence telemetry shows malicious bots have increasingly used AI agent names as cover to probe for secrets, while agents have moved from reading to signing in, booking and buying.

item.title: China-linked actor uses AI agents to exploit zero-day in 11 minutes
item.description: Amazon Threat Intelligence reports a China-nexus actor used Cairn AI agents to discover and exploit a zero-day in a medical imaging app, gaining root access in 11 minutes.

item.title: Webworm suspected of modifying SoftEther VPN to evade detection
item.description: A China-aligned threat actor is suspected of using a customised SoftEther VPN Bridge to hide remote access and bypass security tools.

item.title: Serial-to-IP gateways broadcast lack of authentication to internet
item.description: Research by Flare reveals that a significant proportion of exposed OT serial gateways publicly report that authentication is disabled, creating a direct path for attackers to access industrial machinery.

item.title: WHMCS SQL injection flaw exposes customer data and admin hashes
item.description: An unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability in WHMCS allows attackers to retrieve customer records and administrator password hashes from the platform's database.

item.title: Ox Security: Agent instructions are a new AI attack path
item.description: Analysis of 542,207 components shows prompt injection and tool poisoning are prevalent in MCP servers and agent skills, bypassing traditional code-based security checks.

item.title: Single-bit .NET change bypasses Windows code integrity
item.description: A researcher demonstrated how a minor file alteration allows local attackers to execute untrusted code, bypassing Windows protections and VirtualBox hardening.

item.title: Attackers bypass GitHub SHA pinning via malicious Trivy code
item.description: Threat actors have demonstrated a method to circumvent SHA pinning in GitHub Actions by injecting malicious code into the Trivy scanner that mimics official checkout tools.

item.title: Okta links ShinyHunters-associated vishing group to new INCEPTION data leak site
item.description: Okta Threat Intelligence assesses that a ShinyHunters-associated cluster may have rebranded as INCEPTION, continuing vishing attacks to harvest credentials and approvals.

item.title: FCA warns financial firms on AI agent security risks
item.description: The UK Financial Conduct Authority has issued guidance requiring senior managers to oversee AI agent deployments, warning that failure to manage associated risks could lead to regulatory sanctions.

item.title: AI-assisted campaign compromises Check Point management servers
item.description: GreyNoise reports a threat actor used AI-enabled tools to exploit and maintain persistent access to Check Point Security Management servers across multiple sectors.

item.title: CISA warns of exploited N-able Mail Assure bug
item.description: Federal agencies must patch a critical vulnerability in N-able's email security platform by Thanksgiving after it was exploited to breach company servers.

item.title: Iran-aligned Volant Manticore uses IPFS-based KuboShell backdoor
item.description: A previously undocumented Iran-aligned cyber espionage group has targeted telecommunications, airlines, and critical infrastructure in Cyprus using a new IPFS-based backdoor.

item.title: FulcrumSec claims 9.9 TB exfiltration from Gingko Bioworks
item.description: FulcrumSec claims to have exfiltrated 9.9 TB of data from Gingko Bioworks Holdings, a breach the company acknowledged in October but has not since updated.
